publicPrompt:
Play this logical combination game using only its public interface and rules. Your assignment is the finite collection of all public goals on Windows and redirected light (optics), followed by Impressions, open forms and linings (forms). Revisit either board as needed. Finish when these two boards’ current requirements hold together and their lifecycle achievements have been earned. The other campaign boards are not assigned and need not be completed. Simple or short solutions are welcome. You do not need to use every recipe, demonstrate a particular method, or continue after the assigned collection is complete. You may stop earlier if you prefer; state why. An early stop is a valid test outcome, not a failure to obey.

Work in /workspace/shared/combination-challenge. Read only this setup metadata file, docs/working-materials.md, and output from the public CLI. Do not read implementation, tests, designer or evaluation notes, previous plays, hidden files or other results. Do not run a solver or script future-state search. Select and submit your own game actions; do not delegate construction to an automated policy. You may inspect all public rules, legal actions, requirements and exact single-action previews, and make your own plans. If information is missing or inconsistent, report it rather than guessing what the author intended. Read the public command guide and catalogue before construction. Public information includes recipes, transformations, laws and savedDesigns; do not drop fields when displaying these rules or results. If a tool output is truncated, use lossless chunked display of the same public output, and record exactly which chunks you displayed. You may save public CLI stdout to temporary files solely for lossless display, not action selection or future-state search. Record any display commands and truncation honestly; delivered output and actually displayed output are distinct. Manually selected actions may be submitted in sequence, but do not generate actions programmatically.

Session: fun-materials-v2-early-transform-1. Initialize from that directory with:
node experiments/working-materials-play.ts init fun-materials-v2-early-transform-1 ordinary "$(cat results/working-materials-prompts/fun-materials-v2-early-transform-1.json)"

After initialization, use the public select command to visit optics before your first construction. This navigation does not change your available designs or create any assemblies.

The init output and inspect fun-materials-v2-early-transform-1 cli give the command guide. Commands include view, goals, campaign, inspect, catalogue, partners, preview, combine/act, select, undo, checkpoint, report, finish and verify. All public recipes and requirements are inspectable. The docs/working-materials.md file is a permitted public command/rules guide, not a solution.

Play normally rather than reviewing every move. You need not praise the game or find every action interesting. Plain descriptions of what you did and experienced are most useful.

When all four optics goals are complete, record one brief checkpoint with exactly this question: "What are you trying to do now? Since the last check, what, if anything, was worth doing, and what felt routine or unnecessary?" Record the question and your answer verbatim using checkpoint. Omit the checkpoint if you do not reach this boundary. No per-action explanations are requested.

At completion of the assigned two-board collection or your chosen stopping point, answer this open question using report: "How was the experience as a whole? What would you keep, shorten, remove or change, if anything? What led you to stop here?" Record the question and answer verbatim, then finish and verify the capture. A technical interruption is not a chosen ending; record it honestly rather than inventing a final experience report. Return the session name, actual ending and any technical issue to the coordinator. Your report describes this AI play, not measured human enjoyment or duration.
